posts.title: Building Bridges: Finding Common Ground on Permitting Reform
posts.summary:
We have a rare bipartisan window of alignment to solve this. We already agree on enough to get started. If Congress fails to act, we will fail to deliver for the American people. The market is begging to build. It is time for Congress to stop standing in our own way and get America building again.
Continue reading Building Bridges: Finding Common Ground on Permitting Reform on American Affairs Journal.
bullets: The current U.S. permitting system, centered on the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA), has evolved into a procedural bottleneck that hinders critical infrastructure, including energy transmission, AI-related power needs, and manufacturing.

Data indicates that federal agencies win approximately 80 percent of NEPA litigation cases, suggesting that the primary impact of these lawsuits is project delay rather than the prevention of illegal environmental harm.

Litigation by the ten most active organizations adds an average of 3.7 years to project timelines, creating significant economic and national security risks by stalling essential infrastructure development.

Bipartisan consensus is emerging to reform the permitting process to distinguish between necessary environmental oversight and procedural delays that stifle economic competitiveness and housing affordability.

posts.title: BYD reportedly to take Racco electric K-Car tech global for small EVs
posts.summary:
BYD will repurpose the X-PACK technology introduced in Japan to develop small EVs, with plans to sell them in Europe and other global markets.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: BYD plans to export its X-PACK battery technology, currently used in the Japan-exclusive Racco K-Car, to develop small EVs for global markets including Europe.
The X-PACK system integrates the inverter and electrical components into the battery pack, optimizing cabin space and crash safety for compact vehicles.
The strategy aligns with new EU vehicle categories that mirror Japanese K-Car standards, potentially offering BYD regulatory and subsidy advantages.
BYD may utilize its upcoming Hungary plant to manufacture these small EVs locally, helping to mitigate the impact of EU tariffs on Chinese-made vehicles.

posts.title: China's new rules give smart-vehicle sensors more design freedom
posts.summary:
The new rules provide size exemptions for radar, cameras and V2X antennas, creating more design space for autonomous-driving and vehicle-road coordination hardware.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: China's new mandatory standard GB 1589-2026, effective July 2027, provides dimension exemptions for smart-vehicle sensors like radar and cameras.
The rules aim to resolve conflicts between traditional vehicle size regulations and the hardware requirements for autonomous driving and V2X communication.
The standard also increases the maximum permissible axle load for commercial NEVs to 8,000 kilograms to accommodate heavy battery packs.
New regulations for streamlined semi-trailer tractors and articulated vehicles are designed to support the development of low-drag, energy-efficient logistics vehicles.

posts.title: Momenta posts 76% revenue growth in first results since Hong Kong listing
posts.summary:
Momenta reported a gross margin of 73.2% in the first half, while adjusted loss narrowed to 14.1 million yuan.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Momenta reported a 75.9% year-on-year revenue increase to 1.6 billion yuan in its first earnings report since its Hong Kong listing.
The company achieved a gross margin of 73.2% and significantly narrowed its non-IFRS adjusted loss to 14.1 million yuan.
Mass-production solution installations grew 83.7% to 321,000 units, with the company now serving 26 automakers across 105 vehicle models.
Momenta holds a robust pipeline with 219 cumulative vehicle model nominations, 114 of which have yet to reach the start-of-production stage.

posts.title: Voyah Dream 9 MPV begins pre-sales in China, starting at about $63,420
posts.summary:
The Voyah Dream 9 features Huawei ADS 5 and HarmonySpace 6, along with 4 LiDARs.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Dongfeng's Voyah has opened pre-sales for the Dream 9 MPV, with pricing between 429,900 and 529,900 yuan, positioning it firmly in the premium segment.
The vehicle integrates Huawei's Qiankun ADS 5 and HarmonySpace 6, utilizing a sophisticated sensor suite that includes four LiDAR units for comprehensive autonomous driving coverage.
The BEV variant features a 120-kWh battery, which Voyah claims is the largest capacity currently available in the MPV market, while PHEV versions support 5C ultra-fast charging.
Built on an 800-volt high-voltage platform, the Dream 9 incorporates advanced chassis technology including triple-chamber air suspension and bidirectional rear-wheel steering to enhance handling.
